title: Dividing by two, the wrong way

prereqs.why: Every line is decided by which way integer division rounds, and by the identity that forces `%` to agree with it.

statement:
Say exactly what this prints.

Four lines. Two divisions and two remainders, with the sign on a different operand each time.

The rule to apply is the one C++11 settled, and there is one identity that forces `%` to follow `/` rather than being free to choose.
hints: Integer division in C++ truncates — it rounds towards zero, not towards minus infinity. That settles both division lines on its own.
For the remainders, use `(a / b) * b + a % b == a`. Once you know the quotient, the remainder is not a separate decision.
